name: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
scope: A person with ADVANCED proficiency level in Retrieval Augmented Generation as a competency should be able to / is capable of conceiving, justifying and delivering end-to-end RAG solutions that meet business KPIs, translating fuzzy product goals into phased architectures and budgets. They master vector-space theory, dense-vs-sparse-vs-hybrid retrieval, BM25, probabilistic IR, ANN maths (HNSW, IVF, PQ), transformer attention, hallucination taxonomy, retrieval drift and domain-shift mitigation. They architect multi-stage pipelines—query rewrite → coarse ANN → dense+BM25 hybrid → cross-encoder re-rank → context assembly → generation—using cloud-agnostic microservices with autoscaling GPU/CPU mixes. They fluently configure FAISS, ScaNN, Milvus, Qdrant, Weaviate, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, Vespa, Pinecone, Redis-Vector, AlloyDB-Vector with sharding, memory-mapping, snapshotting and blue/green rollouts. They select or fine-tune embeddings via Sentence-Transformers, OpenAI text-embedding-ada, Cohere, GTE and int8/4-bit or LoRA techniques, balancing dimensionality, recall and latency. They orchestrate with LangChain, Haystack, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, Ray Serve, FastAPI, Triton, serving Llama-2/3, Mixtral, OpenAI, Claude, Gemini on vLLM, DeepSpeed or FasterTransformer with Longformer or Flash-Attention-2 for long contexts. They build ingestion and chunking (semantic, sentence, graph) pipelines, add rich metadata, mask PII, support near-real-time delta indexing, and craft retrieval-aware prompts with citations, chain-of-thought, tree-of-thought and RAG-Fusion. They optimise latency, recall and cost via embedding compression, speculative decoding, caching, early exit, GPU/CPU placement and post-generation re-rank/fact-check/confidence loops. They design evaluation suites—precision/recall@k, nDCG, MRR, BK-score, QAGS, Ragas—and run online A/B or interleaving tests with Prometheus, OpenTelemetry and Grafana while enforcing content filtering, adversarial query detection and ACLs. They ensure governance: copyright provenance, GDPR/CCPA residency, bias mitigation, audit logs, disaster recovery and GitOps-driven Terraform/Helm CICD. They mentor peers, lead design reviews on RAG anti-patterns, liaise with cross-functional teams, publish internal white-papers, contribute to open-source and continually assess innovations like retrieval-augmented tuning, memory-augmented inference, generative knowledge distillation, latent and hyper-retrieval.
long_scope:
Competency: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)  
Target Proficiency Level: ADVANCED (≈ 6–10 years of focused experience)

–––– SCOPE OF COMPETENCE ––––

1. Strategic & End-to-End Ownership  
   • Conceive, justify and deliver RAG solutions that measurably improve business KPIs (search quality, customer satisfaction, cost per answer, etc.).  
   • Translate ambiguous product goals into a retrieval-first system design, articulate trade-offs, and defend architectural decisions to executives, engineers and governance bodies.  
   • Plan phased roll-outs, migration or green-field deployments, budgeting for compute, storage, licensing, monitoring and human-in-the-loop evaluation.

2. Theoretical & Conceptual Mastery  
   • Vector space theory, dense vs. sparse vs. hybrid retrieval; ANN indexing mathematics; transformer's attention mechanism and its implications for grounding generation.  
   • Probabilistic IR models, BM25, language-modelling retrieval, and how retrieval scores compose with LLM likelihoods (e.g., RAG-Fusion, Re-ranking, Fusion-in-Decoder).  
   • Failure modes: hallucination taxonomy, exposure bias, retrieval drift, domain shift; mitigations through retrieval calibration, dynamic context windows, fact-checking loops.  
   • Data governance concepts: PII detection/redaction, license propagation, retention policies in indices.

3. Architectural Design & Pattern Selection  
   • Design multi-stage retrieval pipelines (e.g., query rewriting → fast coarse ANN → dense+BM25 hybrid → cross-encoder re-ranking → context assembly → generation).  
   • Choose indexing schemes (IVF-PQ, HNSW, Flat, Product Quantization variants) aligned with latency/recall constraints.  
   • Architect modular, cloud-agnostic deployments: micro-services or serverless, GPU/CPU mix, autoscaling for ingestion and query workloads.  
   • Integrate retrieval with streaming or event-driven sources, supporting near-real-time refresh, delta indexing, and versioning.

4. Implementation & Tooling Fluency  
   Retrieval Engines / Vector DBs  
     – FAISS, ScaNN, Milvus, Qdrant, Weaviate, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch, Vespa, Pinecone, Redis-Vector, AlloyDB-Vector … able to exploit advanced configs (HNSW tuning, PQ training, memory mapping).  
   Embedding & Encoder Models  
     – Sentence-Transformers, OpenAI text-embedding-ada, Cohere, GTE-family, int8/4bit quantised encoders, domain-adapted fine-tunes; evaluate dimensionality vs. recall.  
   Orchestration & RAG Frameworks  
     – LangChain (custom chains, Memory, Agents), Haystack, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, Ray Serve, FastAPI, Triton Inference Server; implement bespoke pipelines when frameworks fall short.  
   LLM Serving  
     – OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Llama-2/3, Mixtral, custom LoRA-fine-tuned models on vLLM/DeepSpeed/FasterTransformer backends; implement context-window extension (Longformer, RWKV, Flash-Attention-2).  
   DevOps & Observability  
     – Terraform, Helm/Kustomize, GitOps, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Grafana; distributed tracing across retrieval and generation hops.

5. Data Engineering & ETL for RAG  
   • Design ingestion pipelines (batch, micro-batch, streaming); text chunking strategies (semantic, sentence-boundary, graph-based) tuned for downstream token ceilings.  
   • Attach and exploit metadata: semantic categories, temporal signals, ACLs, embeddings version id; support filtered retrieval through attribute or hybrid search.  
   • Automate cleansing: OCR post-processing, language detection, stop-word standardisation, knowledge deduplication, PII masking.

6. Retrieval-Aware Prompt Engineering  
   • Craft prompts that exploit retrieved metadata, citing sources, controlling verbosity, simplifying or multi-step reasoning (chain-of-thought, RAG-Chain-of-Retrieval).  
   • Dynamically select top-k, map-reduce, or tree-of-thought strategies depending on corpus shape and query semantics.

7. Model & Pipeline Optimisation  
   • Quantify and tune latency vs. recall vs. generation quality vs. cost; apply techniques:  
       – ANN index parameter sweeps, GPU vc. CPU placement, tenancy sharding.  
       – Embedding compression (product quantisation, PCA), retrieval caching, pre-generated answer snippets.  
       – Generation cost reduction via distillation, speculative decoding, early exit.  
   • Implement post-generation validation: answer re-ranking, fact-checking with external verifiers, confidence scoring; feed back into retrieval (self-retrieval/fine-tune loops).

8. Evaluation & Guard-Rails  
   • Design offline suites: precision/recall@k, nDCG, MRR, faithfulness/factuality metrics (BK-score, QAGS, Ragas), answer usefulness scoring.  
   • Execute online A/B or interleaving tests; interpret statistical power, confounding factors.  
   • Maintain human-in-the-loop review pipelines; propagate feedback to retriever hard-negative mining or contrastive fine-tunes.  
   • Implement safety layers: content filtering, adversarial query detection, toxic output classifiers, rate limiting, user/auth role enforcement.

9. Scalability & Reliability Engineering  
   • Capacity plan for 10⁵–10⁷ daily queries with P99 < 500 ms; design hot-swap or blue/green index rollouts.  
   • Disaster recovery: index snapshotting, multi-AZ replication, cold start warm-ups, back-pressure mechanisms.  
   • Continuous deployment: canary releases of encoder model or prompt variants, automated rollbacks on KPI regression.

10. Governance, Ethics & Compliance  
   • Ensure copyright compliance, tracking document provenance, implementing source citation in generated output.  
   • Address fairness & bias in retrieval and generation; curate balanced corpora, de-bias fine-tunes, audit logs.  
   • Navigate regional data-residency laws (GDPR, CCPA), on-prem vs. cloud constraints.

11. Mentorship & Cross-Functional Leadership  
   • Guide intermediate engineers on chunking heuristics, embedding selection, index tuning.  
   • Collaborate with product managers, UX, legal, security, and data scientists; convert domain vocabulary into retrievable schemas.  
   • Conduct design and code reviews specifically focused on RAG anti-patterns (over-chunking, naive concatenation, brittle prompts).

12. Continuous Learning & Innovation Horizon  
   • Track emergent techniques: retrieval-augmented tuning (RAT), memory-augmented inference, generative knowledge distillation, latent retrieval, hyper-retrieval.  
   • Rapidly evaluate research prototypes, benchmark on in-house corpora, and decide adoption readiness.  
   • Publish internal white-papers or conference talks; contribute bug-fixes or plugins to open-source RAG ecosystems.

–––– EXPECTED OUTCOMES ––––  
• Production-grade RAG system that achieves high recall (>90 %) and demonstrably reduces hallucination rates.  
• Infrastructure cost curve flattened via index & generation optimisation; clear audit trail of model and data versions.  
• Observable, explainable answers with inline citations and user-friendly fallback behaviour.  
• Organisational capability uplift through documented best practices, internal tooling, and mentoring pathways.

An individual operating comfortably across all of the above dimensions fits the ADVANCED proficiency band in Retrieval-Augmented Generation.

name: AI Evaluation
scope: A person with ADVANCED proficiency level in AI Evaluation as a competency should be able to frame evaluation as a product-quality and risk-management discipline, align metrics with business/user goals, and distinguish between model-level and product-level metrics (accuracy, safety, latency, cost, reliability). They should design and implement robust evaluation strategies for classical ML (using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, ROC-AUC, F1, MSE, NDCG, calibration, and proper splits), and for LLM/generative AI (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, LLM-as-a-judge, preference-based, factuality, robustness, hallucination, prompt sensitivity, long-context, RAG-specific metrics, and code evaluation via unit tests and static analysis). They should create and manage high-quality, stratified, and adversarial test suites, handle data/label quality, and ensure dataset versioning and separation. They must design and run statistically rigorous experiments (offline/online A/B, power analysis, significance testing, control for multiple comparisons), monitor for drift and regression in production, and integrate evaluation into CI/CD and MLOps/LLMOps pipelines using tools like OpenAI Evals, LangSmith, RAGAS, TruLens, DeepEval, Promptfoo, MLflow, W&B, Arize, Fiddler, Evidently, Label Studio, Scale, and annotation platforms. They should manage human evaluation (rubrics, inter-annotator agreement, quality control, ethical protocols), systematically assess fairness, bias, robustness, and safety (demographic slices, stereotyping, adversarial prompts, privacy, truthfulness), and collaborate with legal, compliance, and security teams. They must balance quality with cost/latency, design resource-aware experiments, and communicate results clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders with actionable reports and dashboards. They should document methodologies, metrics, and datasets for auditability, contribute to evaluation governance and process improvement, and mentor others in best practices.

{"sections":[{"name":"Core Evaluation Fundamentals & Mindset","scope_included":"- Frame AI evaluation as a product-quality and risk-management discipline, not just a metrics exercise, and align evaluation goals with business objectives and user outcomes.
- Distinguish clearly between model development metrics (training/validation) and product-level metrics (task success, UX, safety, reliability, cost, latency).
- Define evaluation questions precisely: what is being optimized (e.g., accuracy, helpfulness, harmlessness, faithfulness, robustness), under what constraints, and for which user segments.
- Choose appropriate evaluation paradigms: static/offline evaluation, dynamic/online evaluation, human-in-the-loop evaluation, and hybrid setups.
- Differentiate point-in-time benchmarking from continuous evaluation and monitoring, and define when each is appropriate.
- Reason about trade-offs between different objectives (e.g., quality vs. latency vs. cost vs. safety) and design multi-objective evaluation strategies.
- Separate “capability” evaluation (what the model can do at its best) from “behavioral” evaluation (what it tends to do under real usage) and “risk” evaluation (what it can do at its worst).
- Understand and articulate limitations of evaluation (e.g., incompleteness of metrics, label noise, shifting requirements, proxy metrics vs true goals).
- Critically assess existing metrics and benchmarks for fitness to purpose, identifying where they fail to capture real-world quality or risks.
- Establish clear acceptance criteria, success thresholds, and guardrails with stakeholders prior to experimentation.
- Apply rigorous thinking to avoid common evaluation fallacies: data leakage, cherry-picking, overfitting to the test set, and misinterpreting statistical noise as improvement.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Classical ML Evaluation Foundations","scope_included":"- Apply standard ML evaluation constructs: training/validation/test splits, cross-validation, and proper use of holdout and shadow datasets.
- Use and interpret core classification metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, specificity, sensitivity, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, log loss, Brier score.
- Apply regression metrics where relevant: MSE, RMSE, MAE, R², and understand their behavior under different error distributions.
- Evaluate ranking and retrieval systems with metrics such as precision@k, recall@k, MAP, MRR, NDCG, hit rate, coverage.
- Understand calibration and reliability diagrams; evaluate and improve model probability calibration where relevant.
- Evaluate multi-label and multi-class problems correctly, differentiating micro vs. macro vs. weighted averaging.
- Handle class imbalance explicitly using proper metrics, sampling techniques, and cost-sensitive evaluation.
- Correctly execute hypothesis tests for model comparison (e.g., paired t-test, bootstrap tests, McNemar’s test) when applicable.
- Identify and mitigate data leakage across train/validation/test splits, including temporal leakage, user leakage, and near-duplicate leakage.
- Reason about overfitting to validation/test sets and implement strategies (e.g., nested CV, new holdout creation, periodic re-baselining) to prevent it.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"LLM & Generative AI Evaluation Concepts","scope_included":"- Understand the distinct challenges of evaluating generative models (LLMs, VLMs) compared to supervised models: open-ended outputs, subjectivity, non-determinism, and long-context behavior.
- Differentiate intrinsic metrics (e.g., BLEU/ROUGE-like string similarity) from task- and behavior-centric metrics (e.g., helpfulness, factuality, coherence, safety) and prioritize appropriately.
- Design evaluation strategies for different LLM usage patterns: pure generation, completion, classification via prompting, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and multi-step agents.
- Evaluate LLM-as-a-judge approaches: use of strong models as automatic evaluators, pairwise comparisons, and rubric-based grading.
- Know the strengths, weaknesses, and risks of LLM-based evaluators (e.g., bias, positional preferences, sycophancy, prompt sensitivity) and how to validate them.
- Apply techniques to reduce variance in generative evaluations: multiple samples, majority voting, temperature control, and aggregation strategies.
- Design and interpret preference-based evaluations (e.g., A/B, pairwise preferences, Elo ratings) for generative outputs.
- Evaluate hallucination and factuality: fact-checking strategies, entity-level correctness, support in retrieved or cited sources, and contradiction detection.
- Evaluate instruction-following and alignment with policies or guidelines via scenario-based and adversarial prompts.
- Understand typical generative metrics and concepts: BLEU/ROUGE/METEOR limitations, BERTScore, embedding-based similarity, semantic matching, and task-specific scoring.
- Evaluate prompt robustness: sensitivity to small changes, adversarial or ambiguous inputs, out-of-distribution prompts, and prompt injection attempts.
- Evaluate long-context behavior: reference consistency, information integration over long documents, and degradation with context length.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Task-Specific Evaluation Design for LLM Applications","scope_included":"- Design tailored evaluation schemes for key LLM application categories, each with appropriate metrics and test scenarios.
- Question-Answering & RAG:
  - Evaluate answer correctness, support in retrieved documents, coverage of relevant evidence, and citation quality.
  - Distinguish attribution errors, unsupported statements, missed information, and incorrect information.
  - Measure RAG-specific quality aspects: retrieval recall, precision, context relevance, context compression quality, and faithfulness-to-context.
- Summarization:
  - Evaluate faithfulness, coverage, conciseness, redundancy, topicality, and style constraints.
  - Distinguish extractive vs. abstractive failure modes; detect fabricated details vs. benign paraphrasing.
- Dialogue/Chatbots:
  - Evaluate conversational quality: coherence, turn-taking appropriateness, persona consistency, memory integrity, and user goal completion.
  - Evaluate politeness, empathy, tone adherence, and policy compliance for different user segments.
- Code Generation & Code Assistance:
  - Evaluate functional correctness, type correctness, compilation success, test-passing rate, and code quality attributes.
  - Use unit tests, static analysis, and property-based testing as part of evaluation suites.
- Classification & Information Extraction via LLMs:
  - Evaluate label accuracy, span precision/recall for extraction, schema adherence, and robustness to format variations.
  - Validate structured output (JSON, XML, custom schema) correctness and error types.
- Reasoning & Tool-Use Agents:
  - Evaluate multi-step reasoning correctness, planning quality, tool selection accuracy, and error recovery.
  - Assess task completion rate, number of steps, tool calls, and unnecessary actions.
- Multimodal Systems (if applicable):
  - Evaluate image+text, audio+text, or other modality combinations for alignment between modalities, caption correctness, and groundedness.
- For each application type, design test cases that cover typical, edge, adversarial, and high-risk scenarios, and associate them with targeted metrics and pass/fail criteria.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Experimental Design & Statistical Rigor","scope_included":"- Design robust experiments for comparing models, prompts, and system variants, ensuring reliable and reproducible conclusions.
- Specify clear hypotheses for each experiment, including primary and secondary endpoints and pre-registered decision rules where appropriate.
- Choose appropriate experimental units (query, conversation, session, user) and proper randomization strategies (per-user, per-query, stratified sampling).
- Plan and run offline A/B and A/B/n experiments with sufficient sample sizes, using power analysis or approximations to ensure detectability of meaningful differences.
- Apply appropriate statistical tests and confidence interval estimation depending on metric distribution (parametric vs non-parametric, bootstrap-based methods, Bayesian A/B where applicable).
- Differentiate statistical significance from practical significance and define minimal detectable effect sizes aligned with business impact.
- Control for multiple comparisons across many variants or metrics using techniques such as Bonferroni, Holm, or FDR control when needed.
- Ensure experimental hygiene: guard against p-hacking, data peeking, early stopping biases, and post-hoc metric fishing.
- Analyze heterogeneity of treatment effects across segments (e.g., user groups, query types, languages, difficulty levels) without overfitting to small slices.
- Design and interpret online experiments (when available) that incorporate human behavior, including guardrails for safety and rollback mechanisms.
- Systematically document experiment setup, randomization, sample selection, metrics, and decision criteria to ensure auditability and repeatability.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Data & Test Suite Design for Evaluation","scope_included":"- Construct high-quality evaluation datasets and test suites that faithfully represent intended and real-world usage.
- Define coverage requirements: input distributions, user intents, domain topics, languages/locales, difficulty levels, and risk categories.
- Design stratified test sets that allow per-segment analysis (e.g., by domain, language, complexity, user type) while preserving statistical validity.
- Create adversarial and stress-test subsets to reveal failure modes: tricky prompts, ambiguous inputs, distribution shifts, malicious content, and long-tail cases.
- Design scenario-based and task-based test cases rather than isolated queries, especially for conversations, workflows, and agents.
- Maintain separation between public benchmarks, internal benchmarks, and shadow test sets; ensure that training or fine-tuning data does not contaminate sensitive test sets.
- Manage evaluation datasets lifecycle: versioning, access control, deprecation of contaminated or obsolete test sets, and addition of new coverage.
- Balance synthetic vs. human-curated test data, understanding trade-offs in realism, coverage, and cost.
- Use templating or programmatic generation for scalable test creation while guarding against over-regularity and predictability.
- Label and annotate evaluation data with rich metadata: intent, domain, difficulty, risk level, user persona, and other relevant tags.
- Validate evaluation dataset quality: label consistency, inter-annotator agreement, and absence of systematic bias where feasible.
- For multilingual or localized scenarios, design parallel or comparable evaluation sets across languages, considering cultural nuances and translation artifacts.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Human Evaluation & Annotation Quality Management","scope_included":"- Design human evaluation protocols for subjective or complex aspects such as helpfulness, safety, tone, and user satisfaction.
- Define clear rating rubrics, scales (e.g., Likert, pairwise preference), and examples that minimize ambiguity for annotators.
- Decide when to use expert annotators, crowd-workers, internal domain experts, or end-users; match tasks to annotator capabilities.
- Set up multi-rater schemes, estimate inter-annotator agreement (e.g., Cohen’s kappa, Krippendorff’s alpha), and refine rubrics to improve agreement.
- Calibrate annotators with training rounds, gold-standard items, and periodic quality checks.
- Implement quality control mechanisms: honeypot questions, consistency checks, anomaly detection, and spot audits of labels.
- Combine human ratings with automated metrics and LLM-as-a-judge signals into composite evaluation frameworks.
- Estimate annotation noise and incorporate it into uncertainty estimates for evaluation metrics.
- Ensure ethical and fair treatment of annotators, including reasonable task design, clear instructions, and avoidance of harmful content exposure where possible.
- Handle sensitive content annotation with special protocols, escalation paths, and safety measures.
- Integrate human evaluation into continuous evaluation workflows, balancing frequency, cost, and timeliness of feedback.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Bias, Fairness, Robustness & Safety Evaluation","scope_included":"- Systematically evaluate models for biased behavior across demographic and other protected or sensitive groups where applicable.
- Define fairness-related slices (e.g., demographic attributes, language, region, persona attributes) and design evaluation sets targeting each slice.
- Use fairness metrics appropriate to the task where structured labels exist (e.g., demographic parity, equal opportunity, disparate impact) and adapt concepts thoughtfully to generative settings.
- Analyze group-wise performance disparities and trade-offs, including cases where safety or performance adjustments may impact groups differently.
- Design tests for stereotyping, offensive content, toxic outputs, and microaggressions across demographic categories.
- Evaluate robustness to adversarial prompts, prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, and manipulative instructions, including red-teaming style test sets.
- Evaluate resistance to data exfiltration and privacy breaches (e.g., memorization, re-identification, leakage of secrets) via targeted prompts.
- Assess safety behaviors: appropriate refusals, escalation, guidance toward safe actions, and avoidance of prohibited content.
- Evaluate truthfulness and epistemic uncertainty expression (e.g., honest admission of not knowing, appropriate hedging).
- Collaborate with security, legal, and policy teams to codify safety and compliance evaluation criteria and ensure tests align with policy requirements.
- Interpret fairness, robustness, and safety results responsibly and feed them into mitigation strategies such as prompt changes, filters, or model selection, while documenting residual risks.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Production Monitoring, Drift & Continuous Evaluation","scope_included":"- Design end-to-end evaluation strategies that extend from pre-launch benchmarking to post-launch monitoring and continuous assessment.
- Define online metrics and signals that approximate offline evaluation goals: task success rates, error reports, user satisfaction proxies, safety incident rates, escalation rates.
- Instrument production systems to log necessary data for evaluation: prompts, responses, metadata, user actions, and contextual features with privacy-conscious practices.
- Set up ongoing evaluation pipelines that periodically replay logs through new models or configurations to estimate impact before rollout (shadow evaluation).
- Define and monitor drift indicators: input distribution drift, user intent shift, content domain changes, and degradation in key quality metrics over time.
- Implement automated alerting based on evaluation metrics, thresholds, and anomaly detection for quality and safety regression.
- Design canary and staged rollouts with integrated evaluation checkpoints for new models, prompts, or RAG components.
- Use online experiments (A/B tests, interleaving for ranking-like behavior) when possible and connect results back to offline evaluation outcomes.
- Manage evaluation debt: periodic refresh of test sets, thresholds, and metrics to keep them aligned with evolving product and user needs.
- Maintain a clear framework for rollback or feature gating decisions based on monitoring and evaluation outcomes.
- Integrate user feedback (ratings, flags, support tickets) into the evaluation loop and convert it into structured evaluation signals when possible.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Cost, Latency & Resource-Aware Evaluation","scope_included":"- Incorporate cost and latency considerations as first-class metrics in evaluation alongside quality and safety.
- Define target SLOs/SLAs for latency and availability and integrate them into acceptance criteria for model or system changes.
- Measure and compare token usage, API costs, and computational resource consumption across variants.
- Design evaluation setups that surface quality vs. cost/latency trade-offs, including experiments along parameter axes such as model size, temperature, context length, and prompt complexity.
- Evaluate caching, retrieval optimization, and system-level optimizations (e.g., partial responses, streaming, batching) for their impact on user-perceived quality and latency.
- Consider throughput and scaling behavior when evaluating candidate models or architectures, not just single-request latency.
- Evaluate truncation and context-window strategies (e.g., summarization vs. selection) for their combined impact on quality, latency, and cost.
- Provide stakeholders with clear, quantified trade-off analysis to support model selection and configuration decisions.","is_non_core_section":false},{"name":"Evaluation Frameworks, Libraries & Infrastructure","scope_included":"- Use and extend common AI/LLM evaluation frameworks and libraries to build reliable, scalable evaluation pipelines.
- Work fluently with one or more of the following (or comparable) tools/frameworks:
  - LLM/Prompt evaluation frameworks: OpenAI Evals, LangChain/LangSmith evaluators, RAGAS, TruLens, DeepEval, Promptfoo, or similar.
  - ML monitoring and evaluation platforms: Weights & Biases (including Weave), MLflow, Arize AI, Fiddler, Evidently AI, or comparable systems.
  - Data/annotation platforms: Label Studio, Scale, Surge, Mechanical Turk, Prolific, or internal annotation tools.
- Implement custom evaluators for project-specific metrics: rubric-based LLM judges, heuristics, rule-based checkers, and hybrid metrics.
- Integrate multiple metric types into cohesive evaluation runs: automated metrics, LLM-as-a-judge, human ratings, and system logs.
- Build reproducible evaluation pipelines (e.g., using Python, notebooks, scripts, workflow orchestrators) with configuration-driven runs (YAML/JSON configs) and versioning of datasets, models, and code.
- Manage credentials, rate limits, and quotas when using external model APIs within evaluation pipelines.
- Implement logging, metadata tracking, and artifact storage for evaluation runs to enable later analysis and audits.
- Optimize evaluation infrastructure for cost and turn-around time, including batch execution, parallelization, and caching of model outputs.
- Understand and work within organizational security, privacy, and compliance constraints when setting up evaluation tooling and storing evaluation data.
- Contribute to selecting and standardizing evaluation tools across teams, providing guidance on benefits, limitations, and integration patterns.","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Integration with MLOps/LLMOps & CI/CD for Evaluation","scope_included":"- Integrate evaluation workflows into MLOps/LLMOps pipelines so that evaluations are automated, repeatable, and part of the release process.
- Work with CI/CD systems (e.g., GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, Azure DevOps, CircleCI) to automatically trigger evaluation suites on relevant changes.
- Define evaluation gates and quality thresholds that must be met before deployment, with clear pass/fail signals.
- Use experiment tracking systems (e.g., MLflow, W&B, custom tools) to record model/prompt versions, config parameters, metrics, and artifacts.
- Collaborate with data engineering and platform teams to ensure evaluation datasets are accessible, versioned, and compatible with pipelines.
- Implement reproducible environment configuration for evaluation (e.g., Docker, environment managers), ensuring consistent behavior across environments.
- Participate in designing organization-wide evaluation standards, templates, and recommended practices for teams building LLM-based systems.
- Establish a process for triaging evaluation failures or regressions, assigning owners, and tracking resolutions.
- Integrate evaluation insights into model selection, prompt engineering workflows, and release notes.
- Support creation of dashboards and automated reports that surface evaluation outcomes to engineering, product, and leadership stakeholders.","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Collaboration, Stakeholder Communication & Reporting","scope_included":"- Translate evaluation results into language and visualizations understandable by non-ML stakeholders (product, operations, compliance, leadership).
- Work with product managers and domain experts to co-define success metrics, evaluation criteria, and risk tolerances.
- Facilitate discussions on trade-offs revealed by evaluation (e.g., slightly reduced quality for significant cost savings) and support data-informed decisions.
- Prepare clear, concise evaluation reports that cover methodology, dataset description, metrics, statistical confidence, limitations, and recommendations.
- Communicate uncertainty and limitations honestly, including confidence intervals, potential biases, and external validity concerns.
- Guide cross-functional teams in interpreting evaluation outcomes and in understanding how they translate to user experience and business impact.
- Work with legal, compliance, and risk teams to ensure evaluation practices and documentation meet regulatory or policy requirements where applicable.
- Provide feedback to model developers, prompt engineers, and system architects about systematic failure modes and areas for improvement discovered via evaluation.
- Mentor intermediate or junior team members on evaluation practices, helping them design sound experiments and interpret results correctly.
- Participate in or lead review meetings where evaluation plans and results are presented, challenged, and iteratively refined.","is_non_core_section":true},{"name":"Documentation, Governance & Process Management","scope_included":"- Maintain thorough documentation of evaluation methodologies, datasets, metrics definitions, and decision thresholds.
- Version and track changes to evaluation criteria, test sets, and scoring logic, including rationales for adjustments.
- Contribute to creation and maintenance of evaluation playbooks, runbooks, and checklists for different AI system types (e.g., RAG apps, chatbots, agents).
- Ensure that evaluation documentation supports auditability and traceability, including for safety, fairness, and compliance reviews.
- Participate in or help define governance processes around model changes, ensuring evaluation is a formal gate in change management procedures.
- Record known limitations, open risks, and accepted trade-offs discovered via evaluation so that they are visible and considered in future work.
- Coordinate with security, privacy, and legal teams on policies regarding storage and use of real user data in evaluation.
- Encourage and help implement a culture of continuous improvement in evaluation: periodic retrospectives, metric refreshes, and methodology updates.
- Organize knowledge sharing (internal talks, docs, wikis) on evaluation insights, tools, and best practices within and across teams.
- Ensure that evaluation processes are practical and sustainable, balancing rigor with speed and resource constraints, and adapting them as the organization matures.","is_non_core_section":true}]}

They design and hyper-tune ANN indices, selecting IVF, HNSW, PQ, residual or ScaNN graph variants and tweaking nlist, M, efConstruction, efSearch, quantisation or GPU/FPGA codecs for optimal latency, throughput and memory. They architect and operate sharded, replicated clusters in Faiss, Milvus, Weaviate, Qdrant, Pinecone, Chroma, Vespa, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch k-NN, RedisVector, pgvector or HNSWlib, orchestrated via Kubernetes, Helm and Istio/Linkerd with blue-green or rolling index rebuilds and NUMA-aware placement. Streaming or micro-batch pipelines with Kafka, Pulsar, Airflow, Dagster or Prefect feed embeddings produced by HuggingFace Transformers, Triton Inference Server or TensorRT, ensuring idempotent CDC, versioning, lineage and A/B index swaps. Hybrid vector + boolean + geo queries are surfaced through REST, gRPC or GraphQL, complete with pagination, re-ranking, learning-to-rank loops, ABAC and multi-tenant throttling. The practitioner instruments OpenTelemetry, Prometheus and Grafana for query_latency_p95, memory_fragmentation, index_build_sec and recall_drift while wiring alerts, synthetic probes, snapshots and cross-region failovers to hit 99.9 % availability and tight RPO/RTO. They optimise hardware paths using AVX-512, CUDA tiling, NVMe tiered storage and serverless GPU pools, creating cost models that blend reserved, spot and burstable capacity. Security duties span mTLS/SPIFEE, field-level or Vault/KMS encryption at rest, FHE-friendly ops, IAM-driven ABAC, audit trails and GDPR/RTBF workflows for SOC2 compliance. They integrate vector stores with RDBMS/NoSQL, feature stores, event logs and RAG or semantic-cache layers, guaranteeing transactional or eventual consistency. Continuous innovation includes piloting online-learning indices, adaptive quantisation, new distance kernels and emerging hardware accelerators. Finally, they mentor teams, steer delivery from PoC to GA, conduct architecture reviews and consistently ship billion-vector systems that deliver sub-second SLA with ≥ 95 % recall under controlled cost.

COMPETENCY SCOPE  
Vector Databases – ADVANCED (≈ 6–10 years focussed experience)

An Advanced practitioner is a senior, hands-on technologist who can take complete ownership of vector-database–centric solutions in production, from initial problem framing through long-term operation and optimisation. Depth in the fundamentals is assumed; the distinguishing factor at this level is the ability to deal with scale, performance tuning, distributed deployments, and integration of the vector store as a first-class component of a larger data, ML and application ecosystem.

The scope of proficiency is laid out across the capability dimensions that a Technical Architect must evaluate.

1. Problem Framing & Data Modelling  
• Translate business or research needs into high-level semantic-search / nearest-neighbour retrieval requirements, selecting appropriate distance metrics, similarity objectives and embedding dimensionality.  
• Formalise the vector-native schema alongside complementary scalar / metadata fields, partitioning strategies and hybrid-query plans.  
• Establish statistical evaluation protocols (recall@k, MRR, nDCG, ANN vs exact baselines) and acceptance criteria.

2. Algorithmic Mastery & Index Engineering  
• Select, justify and parameter-tune ANN algorithms (IVF, HNSW, PQ, ScaNN, graph-based, tree-based, product quantisation, residual quantisation, compressed embeddings) in relation to data volume, update frequency, latency and hardware topology.  
• Design multi-index cascades or hybrid indices (vector + inverted + bitmap + Bloom) to support multimodal search, filter-before / filter-after workflows and metadata predicates.  
• Evaluate trade-offs between brute-force, in-RAM ANN, GPU-accelerated, FPGA-accelerated and disk-backed approaches, providing cost-performance models.

3. Distributed & Scalable Architecture  
• Architect sharded, replicated vector-store clusters, defining consistency guarantees, shard selection / routing logic, rebalancing and index build pipelines.  
• Plan for horizontal scaling thresholds (RAM bound, network bound, compute bound) and orchestrate blue-green or rolling index-rebuild strategies to eliminate downtime.  
• Integrate with container schedulers, service meshes and/or serverless GPU pools; design data locality and NUMA-aware placement policies.

4. Performance Optimisation & Cost Engineering  
• Instrument low-level latency profiles (embedding generation, network hop, codec decompression, similarity kernel) to identify micro-optimisation points.  
• Apply hardware-specific tuning (AVX-512, CUDA cores, shared-memory tiling, cache alignment) or adjust algorithmic hyper-parameters (M, efConstruction, nlist, nq) to hit SLA targets.  
• Develop cost projections and autoscaling policies that balance reserved, spot and burstable capacity, leveraging tiered-storage (HBM, NVMe, S3/GCS) where feasible.

5. Data Engineering & Pipeline Integration  
• Build high-throughput ingestion pipelines that perform streaming or micro-batch embedding generation, schema validation, deduplication and index updates.  
• Coordinate with feature stores, message buses and workflow engines (Airflow, Dagster, Prefect) to guarantee idempotency and exactly-once semantics.  
• Manage embedding versioning, back-fill jobs, A/B hot-swap of index versions and lineage tracking via metadata tags or ML metadata stores.

6. Query Processing & Application Interfaces  
• Provide developer-friendly APIs/SDKs, GraphQL extensions or gRPC endpoints that expose hybrid vector + Boolean + geo-spatial queries.  
• Design pagination, cursoring and re-ranking logic to incorporate LTR or cross-encoder feedback loops.  
• Enable multi-tenant isolation, row-level access control and rate-limiting in the query layer.

7. Security, Governance & Compliance  
• Implement encryption in transit (mTLS, SPIFFE) and at rest (field-level, FHE or HE-friendly vector operations when needed).  
• Enforce attribute-based access control for write/read/search paths; integrate with central IAM.  
• Codify data-retention, PII removal and Right-to-Be-Forgotten workflows, maintaining audit trails and SOC2/GDPR alignment.

8. Observability & Operations  
• Instrument custom metrics (query_latency_p95, index_build_sec, memory_fragmentation, recall_drift) and export via OpenTelemetry into monitoring stacks.  
• Build dashboards and alerting rules, schedule synthetic probes for recall regression and fermionic failure modes (OOM, index corruption, hardware faults).  
• Execute disaster-recovery drills, snapshotting and cross-region fail-over, maintaining RPO/RTO commitments.

9. Ecosystem Integration & Interoperability  
• Orchestrate triangulation between vector DB, traditional RDBMS/NoSQL, feature store, event log and ML serving layer, ensuring transactional or eventual consistency where required.  
• Establish ETL/ELT connectors, CDC pipelines or change-vector-capture mechanisms to propagate updates.  
• Provide plug-ins or adapters for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) frameworks, semantic-cache middleware, KG augmentation or multimodal fusion services.

10. Innovation Awareness & Thought Leadership  
• Track the evolution of emerging vector-native storage engines, new distance kernels (cosine-softmax, hyperbolic, spherical), and niche hardware accelerators.  
• Pilot incremental or online-learning adapters, dynamic index updates and adaptive quantisation research, providing actionable adoption roadmaps.  
• Mentor teams, conduct deep-dive sessions, perform architecture reviews and publish internal white-papers or external conference talks.

11. Process & Delivery Excellence  
• Translate fuzzy product requirements into phased vector-search roll-outs (PoC → MVP → GA), creating risk registers and mitigation strategies.  
• Coordinate cross-functional squads (ML, backend, DevOps, SecOps, compliance) and manage backlog prioritisation around data-refresh cadence, quality gates and performance regressions.  
• Conduct post-incident analysis, capacity planning and continuous improvement cycles, embedding learnings into runbooks and playbooks.

Tools, Frameworks & Technologies within expected command (non-exhaustive but canonical for scope justification):  
Faiss, ScaNN, Milvus, Weaviate, Qdrant, Pinecone, Elasticsearch vector features, OpenSearch k-NN, pgvector (Postgres), RedisVector, Chroma, Vespa, HNSWlib; CUDA, Triton Inference Server, TensorRT, HuggingFace Transformers, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus/Grafana, Kubernetes, Helm, Istio/Linkerd, Kafka/Pulsar, Airflow, Terraform, Vault/KMS.

Desired Outcomes consistently delivered by an Advanced-level professional  
• Production-grade vector search or RAG systems that meet sub-second latency under multi-billion-vector scale with ≥ 95 % recall, ≥ 99.9 % availability and clear cost caps.  
• Robust pipelines and index management workflows that absorb continual data drift or concept drift without service disruption.  
• Organisational confidence in the security, auditability and maintainability of the vector-store estate.  
• Uplift of team capability through mentorship, documentation and establishment of best practices.

This scope delineates the competency boundaries: an Advanced practitioner has both deep algorithmic know-how and broad architectural, operational and governance expertise, yet may look to an Expert for frontier research, novel algorithm design, or bleeding-edge hardware co-design.
